title: JobFrame
description: platform.job-frame@1: one job lifecycle frame on the device control link (plan T14 Run; ADR-034 proposed). The link is OpenVibe.Node's WebSocket to OpenVibe.Bot (Node docs/protocol.md section 2); Fabric may terminate it later. Each frame is one JSON object in one text message, with the link's envelope at the top level: `v` (1), `seq` (per-direction counter from 1 on each connection), `ts` (sender's clock, Unix ms) and `type`. Server to device: `job`, `job_cancel`, `job_exit_ack`. Device to server: `job_started`, `job_stdout`, `job_usage`, `job_exit`. The link's existing `ack`/`nack` frames, keyed by the job id, accept or refuse a `job`; a worker that runs jobs advertises its classes in `status.capabilities`. A running `function` job is metered per wall-clock second into platform.usage-sample@1 readings: see `job_usage` and `job_exit`.
$comment: Additive: new frame types and optional fields may extend this v1 contract; a receiver ignores frame types it does not know.

oneOf.description: Server to device: run this job (platform.job@1). Resent until acked; the job id makes a resend harmless.

Server to device: stop this job. A running job's process group is killed and `job_exit` says `cancelled`; a job not yet started never starts; an ended or unknown id is ignored (the ended job's `job_exit` is resent if not yet acked).
Server to device: every usage reading of this job is recorded (written or replayed by Billing), so the worker may forget it and stops resending its `job_exit`.
Device to server: the job's process started. `started_ms` anchors every usage second of the job and never changes.
Device to server: a chunk of the job's stdout, best effort (a chunk lost with the link is not resent; a receiver drops a `chunk_seq` it already has). Never metered.

chunk_seq.description: The job's own chunk counter from 1, across reconnects (the envelope `seq` is the connection's)

oneOf.description: Device to server: wall-clock second `second` of the job has fully elapsed. Metering (platform.usage-sample@1, written through billing.usage.record by whoever terminates the link: OpenVibe.Bot now, Fabric later): second n is [started_ms + n*1000, started_ms + (n+1)*1000) on the worker's monotonic clock. A worker sends `job_usage` for n only once that second has fully elapsed, so every `job_usage` stands for quantity 1; the partial last second is never sent here, only in `job_exit`. Each second is exactly one reading: `id` and `idempotency_key` `run:<job id>:<n>`, `service` `run`, `operation` `function.invoke`, `unit` `s`, `quantity` 1 (the partial last second: (wall_ms mod 1000)/1000, never 0), `at` new Date(started_ms + n*1000).toISOString(), `resource` the job id, `node` the worker's device id, `source` `openvibe-node.worker`, and `project`, `subject` and `provider` from the dispatcher's own record of the job. No field depends on when or how often a frame was sent, and no rating fields (`cost_estimate`, `free_allowance_used`, `vibes_charged`) are set, because Billing keeps the first reading under a key, replays an identical one and refuses a different one (409): a resend after a reconnect, a `job_usage` and the `job_exit` backfill of the same second, and two writers of one job all land on one record.

cpu_ms.description: CPU time used in this second; informational, never billed

oneOf.description: Device to server: the job ended (only after an `ack`). Its `usage` is authoritative for metering: from it the writer writes (or replays) seconds 0 to floor(wall_ms/1000) - 1 with quantity 1 and, when wall_ms mod 1000 > 0, the partial last second, so a lost `job_usage` is backfilled and none is billed twice. Every reason is billed for the seconds the process held. The worker resends the same `job_exit` after every reconnect until `job_exit_ack`. wall_ms comes from the monotonic clock `job_usage` uses, so it is at least (n+1)*1000 for every second n already sent.

reason.description: exited: the process ended by itself; cancelled: `job_cancel`; ttl: `ttl_ms` ran out; limit: a `limits` cap was hit; stopped: the local kill switch or e-stop; failed: the worker could not run it (spawn error, missing artifact)

code.description: The process's exit status; null when it was killed or never ran

result.description: The artifact's declared output (any JSON); null unless reason is `exited` with code 0

wall_ms.description: Running time from `started_ms` to the process's end, monotonic clock; 0 when it never started

started_ms.description: When the job's process started, worker's wall clock, Unix ms
